text:
maria: heads-up: after the 2026-03-17 release we started seeing a spike in compile queue time and token p95 across short-sequence workloads :warning:
kevin: saw that. p95 went from ~22ms to 120ms on canary clusters?
ryan: yup, alert from datadog around 22:12 UTC, also noticed compile storms (huge number of JIT compiles)
sam: any obvious culprit in the deploy?
maria: rolling back test shows perf returns to normal, so likely a heuristic/regression in kernel selector autotune I think
devon: I dug into the logs, kernel-autopick says it switched to matmul-sliced-optim  for batch_size<=4 which is surprising:
```
[2026-03-17T22:11:45Z] kernel-picker: picked=matmul-sliced-optim scores={matmul-sliced-optim:0.87, matmul-block:0.85, matmul-legacy:0.84}
[2026-03-17T22:11:45Z] compile-trigger: missing-variant -> compile(matmul-sliced-optim)
```
kevin: that pick is more expensive to compile for small sequences and causes more kernel builds per-hotpath
ryan: profiling snapshot shows compile_queue: 82% saturated and kv_cache evictions/sec jumped from 30 -> 1100
sam: kv cache evictions? is the kv cache policy also changed in the same PR?
maria: PR #4412 touched both selector scoring and KV eviction heuristic (they were trying to be aggressive on prefix caching)
devon: I ran a micro-repro with short chat workload and forced pick to matmul-legacy -> compile storm disappears, latency stable
ci-bot: perf-ci failure: shortseq_end_to_end_p95 increased by 4.3x for commit abc123 (merged in PR #4412)
kevin: sounds like a mis-scored kernel candidate plus KV policy thrash (cache invalidation causing smaller KV hits -> more work)
ryan: dump from /metrics:
```
runtime.kernel_compile_requests{variant="matmul-sliced-optim"} 742
runtime.kernel_compile_requests{variant="matmul-legacy"} 12
runtime.kv_evictions_per_min 1120
runtime.compile_queue_len 18
```
sam: ok. bisect plan: revert selector change (PR 4412) in canary and see if compile count falls. If yes, narrow to the scoring delta.
maria: created a canary rollback: rollback/4412-canary at 22:30, monitoring now :hourglass:
ops-bot: rollback started on cluster-canary-3 by maria
kevin: while rollback is running, can someone gather autotuner decision traces for the affected model family? need the decision inputs (seq_len, batch, hw info)
devon: attached a small script to collect traces quickly:
```
for id in $(seq 1 200); do curl -s "http://localhost:8080/debug/selector/trace?req=$id" >> /tmp/decisions.log; done
```
ryan: also capture compile cache hits: /admin/compile-cache/stats -> we saw cache miss ratio jump to 0.94 for matmul-sliced-optim
maria: rollback confirmed: metrics trending back to baseline, p95 down to 26ms
ci-bot: perf-ci status: shortseq_end_to_end_p95 reverted to baseline on rollback commit def456
kevin: action items:
- revert PR #4412 permanently and open a follow-up to decouple selector scoring from kv eviction tuning
- add a safety gate: prevent picking highly-compile-heavy kernels for small-batch short-seq hotpaths unless compile cache has stable variant
- add a canary test that simulates rapid short-batch bursts to catch compile storms
- improve telemetry: record selector input features in traces for each compile event
sam: I'll open the revert PR and add a test. putting a temp feature-flag around the new scoring model
ryan: +1 on telemetry, will add a dashboard for compile vs kv_evictions correlated by model and seq_len
devon: logging note: we should store the top-3 candidate scores with the decision to make postmortems easier
maria: thanks all. follow-up sync tomorrow 10:30 to discuss safer autotune rollout checklist :calendar: 
kevin: FYI linking the suspected PR: https://git.redwood.ai/r/redwood/runtime/merge_requests/4412
sam: created revert: MR 4427 -> merging now
ops-bot: MR 4427 merged and deploy started
maria: leaving thread, ping me if rollback doesn't stabilize
kevin: will file a short postmortem once we have the decision traces
__notes: thread contains multiple short messages, code snippets, bot posts; no title field per agents.md
